summary: PED measures how responsive quantity demanded is to a change in the good's own price. It compares percentage changes, so it has no units and can compare goods priced very differently.
key_points: Ratio of percentage changes;No units;Usually negative
key_wording: responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price

summary: PED equals the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price. Work out each percentage change from the original value first, then divide.
key_points: Percentage change = change / original x 100;Keep the minus sign
key_wording: % change in quantity demanded divided by % change in price

summary: Ignoring the sign, a PED above 1 is elastic and below 1 is inelastic. If demand is inelastic, raising the price raises total revenue; if elastic, it lowers it.
key_points: Greater than 1 = elastic;Less than 1 = inelastic;Link to total revenue
key_wording: price inelastic demand;total revenue rises when price rises

summary: PES measures how responsive quantity supplied is to a change in price. Supply is more elastic with spare capacity, stocks, easy entry and a longer time period.
key_wording: responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price

summary: PES equals the percentage change in quantity supplied divided by the percentage change in price. It is usually positive because supply curves slope upwards.
key_wording: % change in quantity supplied divided by % change in price

summary: YED measures how quantity demanded responds to a change in income. Positive YED means a normal good; negative means an inferior good; above 1 means a luxury.
key_wording: % change in quantity demanded divided by % change in income

summary: An indirect tax raises firms' costs, so the supply curve shifts up by the tax. A specific tax gives a parallel shift; an ad valorem tax gives a pivot.
key_points: Specific tax = parallel shift;Ad valorem tax = pivot
key_wording: vertical distance between supply curves equals the tax

summary: The more price inelastic demand is relative to supply, the larger the share of the tax paid by consumers through a higher price. Producers bear more when demand is elastic.
key_points: Inelastic demand = consumers pay more;Elastic demand = producers pay more

summary: A tax equal to the marginal external cost can move output to the social optimum. In practice the external cost is hard to value, and inelastic demand means output may fall little.
key_points: Hard to value external cost;Inelastic demand limits the effect;Revenue can fund alternatives
